Voaters, how do I tactfully resign this week when I have been at a job for less than a year?

I did this recently, here are some tips:

  • write a letter, arrange a meeting with your superior, hand them the letter, let them read it, discuss what you can do to help the transition.

  • make sure that any benefits that are at your superior's discretion are used up before you quit. I had 2 floating "holidays" and they were forfeit the moment i turned over my letter (i had assumed, incorrectly, that they would be treated the same as vacation days).

  • don't tell people where you are going and why it is better.

  • only say positive things about your current job while there, and work like you normally would until the last day.

  • some people would say that you should not tell them the "things they could have done different", the decided not to be competitive for whatever reason.

  • don't allow a counter offer, you will end up quitting even if the money goes up.

If it's not effective immediately, give your supervisor some notice. Say something like "[Boss's name] I want to thank you for the opportunity you've given me to work here, unfortunately I'm putting in my two weeks notice. My last day of work will be [date]." Hopefully your boss will say they're sorry to hear that and direct you to the resignation policy with HR. Some places require written notice and if yours does, just write up a short statement saying "My last day of employment at [company] will be [date]" sign and date it and turn it into HR. You don't have to and shouldn't explain your reasoning for resigning, unless you choose to.

If your resignation is immediate, say something similar "[Boss's name] I want to thank you for giving me the opportunity to work here. Unfortunately, this will be my last day. I am resigning from my position at [company]."

Preferably, you'd want to give some notice as it will help your reputation, your company find a replacement, and generally make the process easier. No matter what, do not feel pressured into giving a reason for your resignation. It's nobody's business but your own and can only make things more complicated.

Submit your official notice (two weeks is normally sufficient) and write some letters thanking various mangers for the opportunity to have worked with them. (great learning experience, great company, great management...etc)
